tier1Summary:
No single event changed South and Central Asia's picture this week, but pressure built at home. In Pakistan the [[p:Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan|TTP]] killed 10 police in Kohat as border skirmishes with the Afghan [[p:Taliban]] went on, and jailed ex-PM [[p:Imran Khan]] needed hospital treatment. Russia sent a large trade delegation to Kabul. India's inflation broke the central bank's 6% ceiling. Nepal's opposition is uniting against PM Balen Shah. Sri Lanka presented its last budget under the IMF programme. Kazakhstan detained the heads of its wealth fund and railway. In the Caucasus, Pashinyan and Aliyev met again without a treaty, and the CSTO sidelined Armenia.

Globally, the White House confirmed a first Trump–Xi–Putin meeting in Shenzhen on 19 Nov, and Kyiv says Europeans will join the next round of Ukraine talks.

segmentItems.text: Militants ambushed police in Kohat, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, killing 10 officers; officials say 18 militants died. The [[p:Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan|Pakistani Taliban (TTP)]] {{note: Militant alliance formed in 2007 in the tribal areas under Baitullah Mehsud.}} claimed it.
Pakistan says it foiled a TTP infiltration in Kurram on 5 Nov and hit [[p:Taliban]] border posts after they fired first. Kabul has not commented.

Jailed ex-PM [[p:Imran Khan]] was taken to hospital overnight on 10 Nov for eye and blood-pressure treatment and returned to Adiala jail, officials say. His lawyer called his blood pressure frightening.

A Russian delegation of 70+ businesspeople under Deputy PM Alexei Overchuk visited Kabul; [[p:Abdul Ghani Baradar]] pitched mining and rail. Trade has doubled this year, Overchuk says. No deals were announced.
October retail inflation hit 6.09%, a two-year high above the [[p:Reserve Bank of India]]'s 6% ceiling; food inflation was 8.94%.

Opposition parties are uniting against PM [[p:Balen Shah]], demanding a parliament session and questioning of the PM, home minister and police chief over a middleman case linked to his office. Ruling-party chair [[p:Rabi Lamichhane]] again questioned the police chief's removal.

President [[p:Anura Kumara Dissanayake]] presented the 2027 budget: higher tax thresholds, the tourism levy scrapped and a 2.3% primary surplus kept, with the [[p:International Monetary Fund|IMF]] programme ending in March. The second-reading vote is on 20 Nov.

[[p:Nikol Pashinyan]] and [[p:Ilham Aliyev]] met at the [[p:European Political Community]] summit in Dublin. They reviewed the US-backed TRIPP rail and road route and a grid link, but announced no treaty signing.

The Russia-led [[p:Collective Security Treaty Organization]] {{note: Military alliance of post-Soviet states; its founding treaty was signed in Tashkent in 1992.}} stripped Armenia of voting rights over unpaid dues but did not expel it.

Hearings on [[p:Georgian Dream]]'s suit to ban five opposition parties resumed on 10 Nov at the [[p:Constitutional Court of Georgia|Constitutional Court]]. Opposition leader [[p:Nika Gvaramia]] says the ruling is predetermined.
The security service detained the heads of the wealth fund [[p:Samruk-Kazyna]] and the state railway [[p:Kazakhstan Temir Zholy|KTZ]] in a corruption probe; no charges have been announced yet.

tier1Check.text: The White House says [[p:Donald Trump]], [[p:Xi Jinping]] and [[p:Vladimir Putin]] will hold their first three-way meeting in Shenzhen on 19 Nov at APEC, on nuclear arms and Iran but not Ukraine. The Kremlin had said Ukraine would come up.
US envoys briefed [[p:Volodymyr Zelenskyy]] in Dublin after meeting Putin: the largest prisoner swap of the war is coming, and Europeans will join the next round. No date has been set.

readInFull.title: Taliban–Pakistan border clashes continue, TTP attack kills 10 Pakistani police
readInFull.why: A dated log of the latest border clashes, drawing on Afghan and Pakistani local media. FDD is a hawkish think tank, so read it for the chronology.

readInFull.title: CSTO Without Armenia: What Keeps Yerevan From Leaving and What the Summit Means for Central Asia
readInFull.why: Analysis of why Armenia stays formally inside the [[p:Collective Security Treaty Organization|CSTO]] while boycotting it, and what the Moscow summit means for Central Asian members.

watchThisWeek.text: Gagauzia People's Assembly and Bashkan elections in Moldova.
Post-election push on the Gaza plan: [[p:Board of Peace]] and [[p:International Stabilization Force]] deployment, plus France's promised conference for the Lebanese army 'after' Israel's election
Whether any Russian diesel cargo is actually delivered to the US under the October arrangement.
Whether Transnistrian leader [[p:Vadim Krasnoselsky]] returns from Moscow and how the five-year exit ban is applied.
Operation Carthage: anti-corruption court rulings on custody for the SBU and police suspects.
Poland: Constitutional Tribunal judges' assembly on lifting Święczkowski's immunity and detaining him.
Washington's reply to Iran's two-day plan and the Qatari-backed draft (day 1: blockade lifted and some funds released; day 2: Hormuz reopens, then nuclear talks).
Iraq: whether more Iran border crossings close under the US Treasury request (Mandali closes temporarily from 13 Nov).
India: [[p:Supreme Court of India|Supreme Court]] hearing on the petitions against the Election Commission's [[e:Special Intensive Revision|voter-roll revision]].
49th ASEAN Summit and related summits in Manila, 16–18 Nov, with Trump attending on 16 Nov: any South China Sea code-of-conduct breakthrough and Myanmar's representation.
APEC in Shenzhen; possible Trump–Xi–Putin meeting on nuclear arms and Ukraine.
House Democratic leadership elections, with [[p:Hakeem Jeffries]] running for Speaker; House Republicans also choose leaders after Mike Johnson stepped aside.
State Duma second reading of Russia's 2027–29 budget.
NATO consultations on letting pilots down radar-tracked drones without visual identification.
COP31 climate conference in Antalya, 9–20 Nov.
UN Secretary-General race: next straw poll, possibly with colour-coded ballots showing permanent-member vetoes.
Moldova's gas-shortage state of emergency expires; watch for an extension and the OSCE-facilitated Transnistria winter gas talks.
Sri Lanka: second-reading vote on the 2027 budget; the final vote follows on 14 Dec.
OFAC licence for Lukoil foreign-asset sale talks expires; possible approval of the Boehly-led bid.
Haitian PM [[p:Alix Didier Fils-Aimé]] visits El Salvador to discuss the future of Salvadoran troops in Haiti.
